pr_title: executor: Fix IndexMergeReader works incorrectly under RC isolation level
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #21151

Problem Summary: When IndexMerge is used in a RC transaction, it may not see the latest committed write, because it forgot 
to refresh forUpdateTS..

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:

The `refreshForUpdateTSForRC` invoking is moved to `getSnapshotTS` function. ~A parameter `forTxnRead` is added to `getSnapshotTS`, and when it's false it doesn't need to refresh it. So for `ChecksumTable` the ts refreshing can be skipped.~ This is a try to avoid forgetting refreshing for update ts for new reader executors in the future.

### Related changes

- Need to cherry-pick to the release branch
  - Release 4.0

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

- Fix the issue that when Index Merge is used in a transaction with RC isolation level, the result may be incorrect.

issue_context.title: buildIndexMergeReader doesn't refresh for update ts in RC isolation level
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

```sql
create table t (id int primary key, value int, a int not null, b int not null,
    index ia (a),  index ib (b));

insert into t values (1, 10, 2, 0), (2, 10, 4, 4), (3, 10, 0, 2), (4, 10, 0, 0);
```
```
MySQL [test]> select * from t;
+----+-------+---+---+
| id | value | a | b |
+----+-------+---+---+
|  1 |    10 | 2 | 0 |
|  2 |    10 | 4 | 4 |
|  3 |    10 | 0 | 2 |
|  4 |    10 | 0 | 0 |
+----+-------+---+---+
```

| session 1 | session 2 | comment |
|-----------|-----------|---------|
|`set transaction isolation level read committed; begin;`| | |
|`select /*+ NO_INDEX_MERGE() */ * from t where a > 3 or b > 3;`| | Returns `(2, 10, 4, 4)` |
|`select /*+ USE_INDEX_MERGE(t, ia, ib) */ * from t where a > 3 or b > 3;`| | Returns `(2, 10, 4, 4)` |
| | `update t set value = 11 where id = 2;` | |
|`select /*+ NO_INDEX_MERGE() */ * from t where a > 3 or b > 3;`| | Returns `(2, 11, 4, 4)` |
|`select /*+ USE_INDEX_MERGE(t, ia, ib) */ * from t where a > 3 or b > 3;`| | Returns `(2, 10, 4, 4)`，latest write become invisible |

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

The last statement above in session 1 should returns `(2, 11, 4, 4)`, because `value = 11` is set by session 2 and session 1 is in a RC transaction.

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

The last write in session 2 is invisible to the last statement in session 1.

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

master (f9f44d0a492a85a9200d9ae476eedfd505db5d7e)



**Note**:

This is caused by not invoking `refreshForUpdateTSForRC` when building IndexMergeReader. It must be invoked when building executors that can access data without nesting other executor.
We'd better have some mechanism to avoid forgetting invoking it.
comments: Also we need to ensure for a single statement it will use the same `forUpdateTS` for example query with subqueries.
I think `refreshForUpdateTSForRC` is reentrant. `IndexMergeReader` is also a basic reader and has exceeded my expectations.

## Please edit this comment or add a new comment to complete the following information

### Bug

Note: Make Sure that 'component', and 'severity' labels are added
Example for how to fill out the template: https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/20100

#### 1. Root Cause Analysis (RCA) (optional) 

For RC transactions, each statement should refresh its read ts. It's implemented by calling `refreshForUpdateTSForRC` when building the basic reader executors. However it's forgotten to invoke when building `IndexMergeReader`.

#### 2. Symptom (optional)

In an RC transaction, if `IndexMerge` is used in a query, it's possible that the query cannot see the latest change make by other transactions.

#### 3. All Trigger Conditions (optional)

* A transaction T is using Read Committed isolation level
* A statement S of T of the transaction uses IndexMerge
* Another transaction commits between transaction T starting and statement S starting, and it modified data that will be read by statement S.

#### 4. Workaround (optional)

Disable IndexMerge.

#### 5. Affected versions

review_comments: Yes. The reason why it's needed is commented in `getSnapshotTS`.
I'm not sure. I think  it's better to keep the additional check before we are sure that this case never happens.

I think we still need this. For some SQLs with a limit statement, although it will be interrupted when required rows are satified. The operator will be canceled step by step(some internal goroutines). It may still under execution. Then the new operators will call `Open` function by `index join`.
Is this case covered by any test?
And by the way, does IndexLookupJoin has the same problem? I found that it didn't force cache the snapshotTS
